hints.title: Find the tangent gradient first
hints.body: Differentiate the polynomial with respect to x, keeping p constant. Then substitute x=−1.
hints.recap: Parameters are held fixed while taking a derivative in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: The constant term <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> has derivative zero.

recall.reminder: Parameters are held fixed while taking a derivative in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Convert to a normal gradient
hints.body: The tangent gradient is −6p2−6p−3. A perpendicular normal has gradient its negative reciprocal, so M=13(2p2+2p+1).
hints.recap: The normal gradient is the negative reciprocal of a nonzero tangent gradient.
hints.pitfall: A reciprocal extremum requires checking the denominator’s sign.

recall.reminder: The normal gradient is the negative reciprocal of a nonzero tangent gradient.

hints.title: Study the denominator
hints.body: Complete the square in the denominator and establish its sign for every real parameter. Then consider how a positive reciprocal changes when its denominator changes.
hints.recap: A positive reciprocal is greatest where its positive denominator is least.
hints.pitfall: Check that a proposed extreme occurs at an allowed parameter value.
hints.pause: Find the denominator minimum, test attainment and obtain the greatest normal gradient.

recall.reminder: A positive reciprocal is greatest where its positive denominator is least.

solution:
With p held constant, f′(x)=−6p2+6px−3x2. At x=−1 this is −6p2−6p−3, so the normal gradient is M=13(2p2+2p+1).

Complete the square: 2p2+2p+1=2(p+12)2+12≥12. Thus the full denominator is at least 32 and never zero. Consequently M≤23.

Equality is attained at p=−12, so the greatest possible normal gradient is 23, option E.
knowledgePattern: Maximise a normal gradient by minimising a positive quadratic denominator
